title: INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM environment variables should not be propagated from plasmashell
line: Apps launched from Plasma no longer inherit Plasma's own INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM; they get their own unit's values or none.
explanation: KIO's systemd launchers copy the launcher's whole environment into the new app: the service runner passes it as the transient unit's Environment=, which overrides the INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM systemd sets for the new unit, and the scope runner forks with it. So every app (and every shell in a terminal) claimed to belong to plasmashell's or krunner's unit and wrote to its journal stream. The change removes both variables in the service and scope runners, so a service gets the values of its own unit and a scope gets none.

commits.message:
systemd runners: don't pass on our INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM

Apps launched as a systemd service or scope got the launcher's own
INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM, so they looked like they belonged to
plasmashell's unit. Drop them, so a service gets the ones of its own unit.

BUG: 487147

media.caption: Konsole launched from Kickoff search has exactly krunner's INVOCATION_ID and JOURNAL_STREAM
With the fix, Konsole has its own values, different from krunner's

review.text: Cleanly strips `INVOCATION_ID` and `JOURNAL_STREAM` in both `SystemdProcessRunner::prepareEnvironment()` and `ScopedProcessRunner::startProcess()`, directly following maintainer guidance in comment #4 so transient services receive their own unit values and scopes do not inherit plasmashell/krunner's. All three launch modes and all 9 launcherjob autotests were verified, and the screenshots confirm Konsole gets its own invocation ID and journal stream.

reviews.text: Cleanly strips `INVOCATION_ID` and `JOURNAL_STREAM` in both `SystemdProcessRunner::prepareEnvironment()` and `ScopedProcessRunner::startProcess()`, directly following maintainer guidance in comment #4 so transient services receive their own unit values and scopes do not inherit plasmashell/krunner's. All three launch modes and all 9 launcherjob autotests were verified, and the screenshots confirm Konsole gets its own invocation ID and journal stream.

Follows David's direction (c4) and matches the title: the systemd service runner (the default on systemd >= 250) no longer overrides the new unit's own INVOCATION_ID/JOURNAL_STREAM via Environment=, and the scope runner drops them; the rig shows Konsole getting its own unit's InvocationID instead of krunner's, and the launcherjob tests pass in all modes. The forking runner is only used without systemd or by explicit opt-out, where plasmashell has no unit values to leak. Shells inside Konsole now see Konsole's own unit values, which is correct systemd semantics; the reporter's wish for them to be unset in terminals is a terminal-side matter (as gnome-terminal does), not plasmashell propagating its own.
